chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad reported to me from Ali ibn al-Abbas, who reported from Abdul Karim ibn Muhammad, who reported from Sulaiman ibn Muqbil al-Harithi, from Mahfooz ibn al-Mundhir, who reported from an elder of Banu Tamim who lived at al-Rabiya.
He said: I heard my father say that they did not know of al-Husayn's martyrdom till the evening of Ashura. I was sitting at al-Rabiya with a man from the district, when we heard a voice saying:

"By Allah, I have not come to you till I had seen at Kerbala, with two dusty cheeks, slaughtered! And around him, young men whose throats spurt blood, like lamps spreading light in darkness. I prodded my camel so that I could meet them before the reticent ones go to meet the Houris. But destiny prevented me, and Allah would fulfil it, and the command of Allah was a determined fate. Al-Husayn was a lamp from which light was obtained. Allah knows that I have never lied. May Allah bless the body which al-Husayn's grave has contained, a companion of goodness, interred. In the neighbourhood of the Prophet in the chambers, and of Ali and al-Tayyar, pleased and satisfied."

So we said: "May Allah bless you, who are you?" He said: "My father and I are Jinn of Nasibayn. We intended to help al-Husayn, peace be upon him, and assist him with our lives. So we proceeded from Hajj but found him killed."

key_terms.جِنِّ نَصِيبِينَ: Jinn of Nasibayn, mentioned in Quran 46:29

ai.seo_question: What did the Jinn of Nasibayn say about al-Husayn's martyrdom at Karbala?
ai.summary: This narration describes how on the evening of Ashura, people at al-Rabiya heard a mysterious voice reciting poetry lamenting the martyrdom of al-Husayn at Karbala. The speaker described seeing al-Husayn's body with dusty cheeks, surrounded by fallen youths whose throats bled like lamps in the darkness. When asked his identity, the speaker revealed himself to be a Jinn from Nasibayn who had intended to help al-Husayn but arrived too late after returning from Hajj.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 7. He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad reported to me from ‘Ali ibn al-Abbas, who reported from Abdul Karim ibn Muhammad, who reported from Sulaiman ibn Muqbil al-Harith, who reported from Mahfooz ibn al-Munzar, who reported from an elder of Banu Tameem, who lived at al-Rabiya.
He said: I heard my father say that they did not know of al-Husayn’s martyrdom till evening of Ashura.

He said: I was sitting at al-Rabiya with some people from that district, and we heard a voice saying: "By Allah, I have not come to you till I had seen at Kerbala, the head cut off, with two dusty cheeks! And around him, young men whose throats spurt out blood, and like lamps spreading light in the darkness. I prodded my camel (to run) so that I could meet them before the reticent ones go to meet the Houris. But the destiny prevented me, and Allah would fulfil it, And the command of Allah was a determined fate. Al-Husayn was a lamp from which light was obtained. Allah knows that I have never lied, May Allah bless the body, which has been contained by al-Husayn’s grave, as a good companion. In the neighbourhood of the Prophet in the chambers, and of ‘Ali and al-Tayyar, pleased and satisfied."

So we said: "May Allah bless you with mercy, who are you?" He said: "My father and I are Jinn of Nasibayn. We intended to help al-Husayn, peace be upon him, and assist him with our lives. So we proceeded from Haj, but reached him when they had been killed.
